newsitem.title: USA: FERC seen likely to clear Duke, PanEnergy merger.
newsitem.headline: FERC seen likely to clear Duke, PanEnergy merger.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission is likely to approve the merger of Duke Power Co with PanEnergy Corp when it considers the proposal Wednesday, industry experts said Tuesday.

Analysts and attorneys said they saw no reason for the FERC to reject the $7.7 billion union of the big electric utility with the natural gas marketer and pipeline company, since their territories do not overlap.

"PanEnergy doesn't have a contiguous geographic monopoly. It doesn't really give Duke more market pwer, in the sense of dominant market power," said Roger Gale, president of Washington International Energy Group.
The potential for a company to dominate a market is the key issue that the commission looks at when reviewing merger cases under its new merger policy.
The plan to form Duke Energy is very different from the proposed merger of Wisconsin Energy Corp and Northern States Power to form Primergy, which FERC commissioners rejected two weeks ago.

"I don't see the same type of market power issues that they were troubled by...in the Primergy case present in this case," said former FERC general counsel William Scherman, a partner at Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom.
The Duke Energy proposal is the second so-called convergence merger, involving an electric utility and a natural gas company that the FERC has considered.
The commission earlier this year approved the marriage of natural gas giant Enron Corp with the utility Portland General.
In this case there are even fewer questions than in the Enron-Portland General case because PanEnergy has no pipelines in Duke's service area -- North Carolina and South Carolina.
"We're cautiously optimistic that the news will be good (at Wednesday's FERC meeting,)" said Duke Power spokesman Randy Wheeless.
